Q1: Zinc chloride exhibits a comprehensively characterized hazard profile with most categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental, inhalation, oral, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic hazards, classified as Tier 1. This indicates known, significant hazards officially recognized by the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Endocrine disruption hazards (EDC) are rated as Tier 2, reflecting an expanded perspective beyond GHS through current scientific data.
Q2: Zinc chloride is identified on two significant "Lists of Concern." It is included on the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor, indicating evidence of endocrine disruption in scientific research. Additionally, it is listed under the Clean Water Act, signifying its environmental regulatory status.
Q3: Zinc chloride is exceptionally well-characterized, supported by an extensive body of scientific literature with 78,000 references, far exceeding the median for similar chemicals.
